record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis directly in superspace for supersymmetric integrable systems, so that the superspace formulation itself supports the same structural insights that the ordinary Painlevé test gives for integrable equations, including access to objects such as Bäcklund transformations and Lax operators?

evidence.quote: There are further general questions that could be formulated in relation with super integrable systems. As stressed here, these equations are naturally formulated in superspace. Over the years, it became clear that a lot of structure is contained in the Painlevé test: for instance its truncation leads to Backlund transformations and the Lax operator [20]. Yet, no Painlevé analysis has been done directly in superspace. OP-7: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis in superspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The classical Painlevé test for an ordinary nonlinear partial differential equation u_t = K(u, u_x, u_xx, ...) studies movable singularity expansions u(x,t) = sum_{k>=0} u_k(x,t) (φ(x,t))^{k-α} about an arbitrary noncharacteristic singular manifold {φ=0}; the equation is said to pass the Painlevé test if such expansions exist with the correct number of arbitrary functions among the u_k. The truncation of these expansions yields, among other structural objects, Bäcklund transformations and Lax pairs for integrable equations.

In supersymmetric integrable systems, the dependent variables are naturally combined into a superfield Φ(x,t,θ) (or Φ(x,t,θ_1,...,θ_N) in the N-extended case), where θ, θ_i are anticommuting (Grassmann) coordinates, and the dynamics are formulated covariantly in the superspace with supercovariant derivatives D = ∂_θ + θ ∂_x. So far, Painlevé analyses of supersymmetric equations have proceeded only after projecting the superfield onto its component bosonic and fermionic fields (or after bosonization), so the test is carried out in ordinary space rather than directly in superspace.

Problem. Formulate a Painlevé singularity analysis directly in superspace, i.e. devise a notion of movable singular supermanifold {Φ_sing = 0} (with Φ_sing a superfield depending on x, t, and the Grassmann coordinates) and a corresponding Laurent-type expansion of the superfield solution in powers of an appropriate superspace "distance" function, such that:
(a) the test can be applied covariantly to any supersymmetric integrable system (for example the N=1 and N=2 supersymmetric KdV hierarchies) without first reducing to components;
(b) the resonance analysis and the freedom of arbitrary superfunctions parallel those of the ordinary Painlevé test; and
(c) truncation of the superspace expansion produces, in manifestly supersymmetric form, the Bäcklund transformations and Lax operator associated with the system.

Either construct such a superspace Painlevé analysis with the required structural consequences, or prove that no such covariant superspace formulation with these properties can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: Painlevé analyses have been carried out for supersymmetric integrable systems such as the N=1 and N=2 super KdV equations and the supersymmetric Ito equation, but these proceed either via component decomposition of the superfields or via bosonization (replacing fermionic fields by Grassmann-parameter-dressed bosonic fields). I did not find a published formulation that performs the Painlevé test fully covariantly in superspace with movable singular supermanifolds and superspace truncation yielding manifestly supersymmetric Bäcklund transformations and Lax operators. The question thus appears to remain essentially open in its original superspace-covariant form, though related component-level and bosonized analyses constitute partial progress.

status_evidence.title: The Painlevé analysis for N=2 super KdV equations
status_evidence.snippet: Painlevé analysis of N=2 extensions of KdV, performed at the level of component fields with two fermionic fields.
status_evidence.claim: Painlevé analysis for supersymmetric KdV has been carried out via components, not directly in superspace.

status_evidence.title: Bosonization, singularity analysis, ... of supersymmetric KdV equation
status_evidence.snippet: Using singularity analysis, the Painlevé property of bosonized SKdV systems is proved and Bäcklund transformations are found.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity analysis of SUSY KdV proceeds via bosonization rather than directly in superspace.

status_evidence.title: Painlevé integrability of the supersymmetric Ito equation
status_evidence.snippet: The supersymmetric Ito system is shown to pass the Painlevé test using Kruskal's simplified method.
status_evidence.claim: Further Painlevé tests of SUSY systems use component-level / Kruskal techniques.
